title: HB402 (2018 Regular): Public Safety – Firearms Disqualifications – Antique Firearm\r (Shadé’s Law)

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2018RS/bills/hb/hb0402f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader (as filed, January 24, 2018; "Shadé’s Law"); no enrolled text was read. The bill deletes the old § 5-205(a), which said the subtitle does not apply to antique rifles or shotguns, and adds a new (A) defining "antique firearm". No passage vote is recorded.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-205(a)): IN THIS SECTION, “ANTIQUE FIREARM” HAS THE MEANING STATED IN § 4–201 OF THE CRIMINAL LAW ARTICLE.

Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-205(d)): A person who violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction is subject to imprisonment not exceeding 3 years or a fine not exceeding $1,000 or both.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-205(e)): A person who is disqualified from owning a rifle, A shotgun, OR AN ANTIQUE FIREARM under subsection (b)(6), (7), (8), (9), (10), or (11) of this section may seek relief from the disqualification in accordance with § 5–133.3 of this title.
